A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MolJO and retain corresponding methods, proofs, experiments, and appendices despite the changed title and layout. All 27 pages of each version support comparison; visual inspection resolves table-extraction problems.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrossDocked2020 optimization results, constrained molecule-design experiments, ablations, conformation analyses, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds sampling comparisons, selection analyses, and statistical evaluations. Some additional baseline scores are explicitly attributed to other authors.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 1 specifies discrete guidance through the latent gradient -grad_y E. v3 Algorithm 1 and Section 4.2 instead specify parameter-space gradients and explicitly bypass the derivative from discrete parameters to latents. This is a limited refinement of the stated guidance procedure; the backbone, objectives, and backward-correction framework remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use CrossDocked2020 for unconstrained property optimization, R-group redesign and growing, scaffold hopping, and larger-molecule evaluation. The CBGBench-sourced baseline rows do not establish additional data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: AutoGrow4 enters the main property comparison in v3 Table 1, having previously appeared only in the runtime comparison. New Table 10 compares DiffBP, D3FG, VoxBind, and DecompDPO. Table 4 adds SDE sampling and removes its separate Vanilla MC and Full B.C. rows, substantially broadening and revising the evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds a common top-of-N protocol selecting the highest-ranked tenth of each included baseline's samples, whereas v1 reports this selection only for MolJO. The sampler comparison additionally evaluates Vina Dock. Appendix D.1 changes the stated regressor learning rate from 0.005 to 0.0005; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new top-of-N analysis tests performance after applying common oracle-based screening, and the revised sampler ablation tests backward correction against SDE guidance. Existing modality, correction-window, guidance-scale, objective-combination, molecular-size, and conformation analyses largely remain. Removing the joint-guidance bar chart does not remove its underlying tabulated ablation.

E5.justification: v3 introduces 95% confidence intervals for main-result metrics in Table 6 and pairwise t-tests against Vanilla and SDE guidance with N = 1000 in Table 12. Table 16 also identifies the existing runtime error bars as standard deviations across ten proteins. These substantially extend statistical reporting but do not establish additional independent training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Substantial new result sets cover additional baselines, top-of-N selection, and SDE sampling. For example, v3 reports AutoGrow4's 14.3% success rate and top-of-N success rates of 55.0% for MolCRAFT and 70.3% for MolJO. Headline MolJO results remain unchanged. New Table 6 also contains unexplained comparator means differing from retained Table 1, such as DecompOpt Vina Dock -8.425 versus -7.63; these cannot be interpreted as established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the continuous-gradient correspondence in Remark 4.2: Equation 7 includes the squared rho_i/alpha_i factor missing from v1 Equation 8. This changes mathematical reasoning beyond notation. The principal guidance and equivariance propositions and their appendix proofs otherwise remain substantially the same.

C1.justification: v3 removes the repeated claims that MolJO is the first gradient-based or first joint gradient-based SBMO framework and the first proof of concept for continuous-discrete optimization. The joint-guidance, backward-correction, application, and headline performance contributions remain, narrowing the priority claim without redefining the work.

C2.justification: v3 adds discretization error as a possible explanation for SDE guidance's behavior and interprets the common-selection results as evidence of optimization efficiency. It removes v1 Appendix J's explicit limitation to three objectives and its discussion of missing biologically meaningful objectives such as ADMET. Most existing mechanism explanations and qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents posterior sampling formulas for regressor training, supplies the top-of-N ranking formula and normalization, and explicitly states ten samples per test protein for the ablations. It also revises the reported learning rate and identifies the provenance of additional baseline results. Backbone architecture, hardware, training duration, and principal sampling settings remain documented as before.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning relative to SDE-based BFN sampling, DiffAC policy-gradient optimization, and CBGBench's constrained graph-completion framework, alongside references supporting the added comparisons. The introduction now recognizes DiffSBDD's evolutionary optimization and presents gradient guidance as orthogonal to such resampling. The broader related-work narrative remains.

P1.justification: The title changes, prose is locally tightened, parameter notation is standardized to theta superscripts, and Algorithm 1 is shortened through equation references. Acknowledgments are added, and standalone reproducibility and limitations sections disappear. Most prose and the main section progression are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and redistribution of figures and tables. v3 adds confidence-interval, top-of-N, additional-baseline, and t-test tables and restructures Table 4. The distribution-shift figure moves to the appendix, while the joint-guidance bar chart is removed with its tabulated evidence retained.

improvement.justification: The common top-of-N comparison and SDE comparator improve assessment of the optimization advantage, while the corrected gradient relation and fuller technical documentation improve precision. These gains are limited by unexplained discrepancies between the new confidence-interval table and the retained main results, and by removal of the explicit three-objective/ADMET limitation. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
